title: 暮江吟
titleEn: Song of the River at Dusk
author: 白居易
intro: Sunset on a river, then nightfall: half the water turns jade-green, half glows red, and later dew shines like pearls under a moon thin as a bow. Four lines, two pictures, all colour.
analysis: 这首诗写一个秋天的傍晚到夜晚，在江边看到的景色。前两句写黄昏：最后一道夕阳斜斜地照在江面上，用“铺”字，好像把阳光平平地铺在水上。照到阳光的一半江水是红的，没照到的一半是碧绿色（“瑟瑟”本是一种绿色宝石，这里指碧绿色）。“半江瑟瑟半江红”一句里有两种颜色，画面非常鲜明。后两句写入夜：诗人说九月初三的夜晚真可爱（“可怜”在古代是“可爱”的意思），草上的露水像一颗颗珍珠，弯弯的新月像一张弓。两个比喻都很简单、很准确。全诗从黄昏写到夜里，时间在流动，诗人一直舍不得离开，他的轻松愉快就藏在这些景色里。
analysisEn: This poem follows one autumn evening on a riverbank, from sunset into night. The first two lines are dusk: the last band of sunlight lies across the river, and the verb 铺 (“to spread out”, as you would spread a cloth) makes the light look laid flat on the water. Where the sun touches, the river is red; where it doesn’t, the water is a deep blue-green — 瑟瑟 was the name of a green gemstone. “Half the river jade, half the river red” puts two colours side by side in one line. The last two lines are nightfall. The poet calls the night of the third day of the ninth month 可怜 — in classical Chinese this means “lovely”, not “pitiful” as it does today. Dew on the grass looks like real pearls, and the new moon is curved like a bow. Both comparisons are simple and exact. Time moves through the poem from sunset to night, and the poet clearly can’t bring himself to leave; his quiet happiness is hidden in the scenery.
background: Bai Juyi (772–846) was among the most widely read Tang poets. This poem is traditionally dated to about 822, when he left the troubled politics of the capital to become governor of Hangzhou — which may explain its light, relaxed mood.
pronunciation: 铺 pū（铺开），不读 pù；瑟瑟 sè sè；可怜 kě lián（古义“可爱”）。
version: 采用统编语文教材（四年级上册）文本。“真珠”即珍珠，教材作“真珠”，有的版本写作“珍珠”。

lines.py: yī dào cán yáng pū shuǐ zhōng
lines.lit: One band of the setting sun spreads across the water;
lines.en: A last ribbon of sunset lies spread across the water —

lines.py: bàn jiāng sè sè bàn jiāng hóng
lines.lit: half the river jade-green, half the river red.
lines.en: half the river jade-green, half the river aflame.

lines.py: kě lián jiǔ yuè chū sān yè
lines.lit: Lovely is the night of the ninth month’s third day:
lines.en: How lovely, this third night of the ninth moon:

lines.py: lù sì zhēn zhū yuè sì gōng
lines.lit: dew like real pearls, the moon like a bow.
lines.en: dewdrops like pearls, and a moon bent like a bow.

words.note: 古诗的一种体裁名；现代汉语“吟诗”“沉吟”。
快落山的太阳，书面语；现代汉语说“夕阳”。
现代汉语“铺床”“铺开”；读 pù 是“店铺”。
本是一种碧绿的宝石，这里指碧绿色；今天“瑟瑟发抖”是另一个意思（发抖）。
古义“可爱”；今天的“可怜”是 pitiful，意思完全不同。

words.en: the third day (of a lunar month)
words.note: 农历每月的第三天，今天仍这样说；这天的月亮是细细的新月。
即“珍珠”，现代汉语写“珍珠”。

imagery.name: 夕阳
imagery.zh: 夕阳平铺在江面，把江水染成一半红一半绿，是全诗最鲜艳的画面。
imagery.en: The low sun lies across the river and splits it into red and green — the brightest picture in the poem.

imagery.name: 江
imagery.zh: 江面像一块画布，先映出夕阳的颜色，后来又托起夜色。
imagery.en: The river is like a canvas: first it holds the colours of sunset, then the darkness of night.

imagery.name: 露
imagery.zh: 露珠像珍珠一样闪亮，说明已是深秋夜晚，也写出诗人看得入迷、待得很久。
imagery.en: Dewdrops shining like pearls: it is a late-autumn night, and the poet has stayed long enough to see the dew form.

imagery.name: 月
imagery.zh: 初三的新月细细弯弯像一张弓，清新可爱，没有思乡的愁。
imagery.en: The thin new moon curved like a bow — fresh and charming, with none of the usual homesick sadness.
